next_step: Closed-lost. Add to Q4 re-engagement cadence; prepare migration ROI for post-contract review.
notes:
Outcome: Closed-lost to Azure managed endpoints (Azure OpenAI + integrated AAD endpoints).

Deal summary: Ceres was vetting Redwood for low-latency ad-ranking and realtime creative chat assistants. They ran a 3-week POC; Redwood met latency and quality SLOs. Despite technical fit, procurement and infra opted for Azure-managed endpoints to consolidate on the existing enterprise Azure commitment.

Signals / call highlights:
- CTO: 'We need everything under our Enterprise Agreement and AAD integration is non-negotiable.'
- Procurement pushed back on vendor count; Azure offered consolidated billing and a 25% committed discount for model endpoints.
- Security liked Redwood audit logs but prioritized native AAD audit trail + centralized key rotation via Microsoft Key Vault.
- Internal ML lead (Ravi Patel) initially championed Redwood but was moved to growth team mid-POC; no replacement champion.
- There was a one-week price negotiation; Azure countered with dev credits + migration support.

POC & activity timeline:
- 2025-10-10: Discovery (Avery) - requirements: <50ms p95 for ranking path, embeddings for similarity.
- 2025-11-02: SE deep-dive (Diego) - demoed VPC peering, prefix caching benefits.
- 2025-11-18: POC kickoff (ad-ranking microservice + creative chat).
- 2025-12-08: Security questionnaire sent; requested Key Management alignment.
- 2026-01-07: Mid-POC review - performance good; finance requests comparative TCO.
- 2026-01-29: Azure commercial offer surfaced (discount + integration incentives).
- 2026-02-14: Internal champion moved teams; engagement drops.
- 2026-02-25: Final decision: select Azure-managed endpoints.

Why lost (short):
- Hyperscaler lock-in preference: one bill and simplified operations via Azure EA.
- Commercial: Azure committed discount + credits made short-term TCO lower.
- Org change: loss of internal champion halts momentum.
- Security: perceived lower integration lift with native Azure KMS/AAD flows.

Actions taken by Redwood team:
- Provided detailed architecture docs and migration plan (drive link).
- Offered a Dedicated pricing revision and transition support.
- Engaged Field Engineering for a technical deep-dive with security stakeholders.

Recommended follow-ups / recovery plan:
- Mark closed-lost; set reminder for 9 months (post-Azure contract review) to re-open conversation.
- Create a short one-page comparison: 'Redwood vs. Hyperscaler: multi-year TCO and vendor diversification'.
- Target new champions in Platform Engineering and Procurement; call out hybrid routing benefits (cost/fallback).
- Maintain lightweight monthly newsletter to contact lists; watch for re-org signals.
